study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Yu et al., Human Brain Mapping, 2024
study_identification_part.si4_title: Behavioral and brain morphological changes before and after hemispherotomy

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: This study systematically investigated changes in gray matter volume (GMV) before and after hemispherotomy surgery in pediatric patients and analyzed relationships between GMV changes and behavioral recovery, as well as whether preoperative GMV features can predict postoperative behavioral outcomes.

rci1_dataset_name.answer: Multi-site aggregated dataset; representative: ABIDE I; ABIDE II; BCP; CPMD; CBD; CCNP; HBN; HCPD; IBIS; PeriCBD; PING; Pixar
rci1_dataset_name.reason: The study explicitly lists all 11 datasets used for normative modeling. These are detailed in both the main text and supplementary materials. Since there are 11 datasets (more than 5), following the extraction guidance, I listed them all with the multi-site qualifier.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: Here, the healthy subjects used for normative model estimation were from 11 MRI datasets, including the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (Di Martino et al., 2014; Di Martino et al., 2017), the UNC/UMN Baby Connectome Project (Howell et al., 2019), the Calgary Preschool MRI Dataset (Reynolds et al., 2020), the Children School Functions and Brain Development Project (Lei et al., 2022), the Chinese Color Nest Project (Liu et al., 2021), the Healthy Brain Network (Alexander et al., 2017), the Human Connectome Project-Development (Harms et al., 2018), the Infant Brain Imaging Study (Lewis et al., 2017), the Multicenter Database on Perinatal Factors in Child Brain-Mind Development (Wang et al., 2024), the Pediatric Imaging, Neurocognition, and Genetics (Jernigan et al., 2016), and the Pixar Dataset (Richardson et al., 2018)

The initial sample was 2343 children aged 0.3-13.0 years, but 228 were excluded due to poor image quality or processing failure, resulting in 2115 healthy children used for normative modeling.
rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: Given the age range of the hemispherotomy patients (0.6 -11.6 years old), we included T1-weighted images from all healthy children aged between 0.3 and 13.0 years across these datasets, with a maximum of 100 subjects for a half-year interval (in total 2343 children). For children with multiple T1-weighted images, only the image of the highest quality was used. This ensured independency of all included images. Among these images, 228 were excluded due to poor image quality or image processing failure. VBM processing was then applied to the remaining 2115 children

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.answer: SPM12; Symmetric T1 template in MNI space; Serial Longitudinal Registration toolbox; Voxel-based morphometry (VBM); Segmentation into GM, WM, CSF probability maps; Modulated with twofold Jacobian determinants; 8-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel smoothing
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: The paper provides detailed description of the VBM preprocessing pipeline using SPM12, including longitudinal registration, segmentation, normalization to a symmetric template, modulation, and smoothing steps.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: we carried out voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses using SPM12. To ensure unbiased comparisons between the two hemispheres, a symmetric T1 template in MNI space was constructed using 2115 healthy children... Longitudinal VBM processing included the following. (1) For each patient, an average image across the longitudinal images was generated using the Serial Longitudinal Registration toolbox (Ashburner & Ridgway, 2013). (2) The average images were bias-corrected and segmented into GM, WM, and cerebrospinal fluid probability maps... (3) The GM probability maps were then modulated with twofold Jacobian determinants... (4) Finally, all raw GMV images were smoothed with an 8-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel.

rci8_quality_checking.supporting_text: Initially, 74 patients met these criteria, but the image processing procedures failed for 17 of them due to the poor quality of either pre- or postoperative MRI images (e.g., severe head motion, bad intensity contrast, abnormalities and severe distortion of the unaffected regions). Finally, 29 pediatric patients with left hemispherotomy and 28 pediatric patients with right hemispherotomy were included in our analyses... The resultant images of each step were carefully checked by visual inspection... Notably, distinguishing between GM and WM boundaries on T1w images of babies is difficult (Boshuisen et al., 2010). We carefully examined the T1 images of our patients, particularly at younger ages, and excluded those with poor contrast... The Gaussian process regression approach may implicitly capture some variance, but this is not explicitly stated as addressing site effects.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Linear mixed-effects models (LMEMs) with 'MRI to surgery' time and covariates (onset of epilepsy, age at surgery, etiology, and sex for behavioral analysis) as fixed effects and individual identities as random effects; voxelwise LMEM for GMV changes with random field theory correction (uncorrected p<.001, corrected p<.025 accounting for 2 patient groups); Pearson correlation between GMV change and behavioral score change within identified clusters; machine learning prediction models (SVR, LASSO, ridge regression) with nested leave-one-out cross-validation to predict postoperative behavioral scores from preoperative GMV; permutation tests (1000 iterations) for model significance; Wilcoxon signed-rank test comparing prediction performance between groups; FDR correction for feature importance maps
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Both left and right hemispherotomy patients showed widespread GMV increases in contralateral cerebrum and ipsilateral cerebellum but decreases in contralateral cerebellum; GMV decrease in contralateral cerebellum correlated with behavioral improvement only in right hemispherotomy patients (r=-0.64, p=.007); preoperative GMV features significantly predicted postoperative behavioral scores in both groups.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Both patient groups showed consistent patterns of GMV changes: (1) widespread GMV increases in contralateral cerebrum (left: t=6.92, p<.001; right: t=7.44, p<.001) and ipsilateral cerebellum (left: t=6.95, p<.001; right: t=8.53, p<.001); (2) GMV decreases in contralateral cerebellum (left: t=-8.32, p<.001; right: t=-7.73, p<.001); (3) additionally, left hemispherotomy showed GMV decrease in contralateral cingulate gyrus (t=-5.23, p<.001). The contralateral cerebellar GMV decrease significantly correlated with behavioral improvement in right (r=-0.64, p=.007) but not left (r=-0.10, p=.73) hemispherotomy patients. Machine learning models successfully predicted postoperative behavioral scores from preoperative GMV with significant correlations (left group: RR r=0.52, p=.006; right group: RR r=0.48, p=.021), with better performance in left than right hemispherotomy patients. Feature importance maps differed substantially between groups, with left patients showing contributions from bilateral cerebellum and contralateral occipital lobe, while right patients showed contributions from bilateral cerebellum and contralateral temporal lobe. Both groups showed significant behavioral improvement post-surgery (left: t=2.10, p=.04; right: t=3.97, p<.001), with 90% of left and 100% of right patients achieving Engel I seizure outcome.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Small absolute sample size despite being relatively large for hemispherotomy studies; limited number of training subjects for machine learning algorithms affecting confidence in validity and generalizability; need for external validation from different hospitals/sources; difficulty in distinguishing GM/WM boundaries in younger pediatric patients
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: However, it should be noted that the absolute sample size of patients is small, although the relative sample size for hemispherotomy patients was quite large for an investigation in hemispherotomy. Particularly, the number of training subjects for the machine learning algorithm is small, limiting the confidence in the validity and generalizability of the prediction. A larger dataset of pediatric hemispherotomy patients (e.g., from different hospitals or sources) are warranted to further validate our currently proposed machine learning-based prediction... Notably, distinguishing between GM and WM boundaries on T1w images of babies is difficult

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Study separated left and right hemispherotomy patients for all analyses due to known hemispheric specialization and asymmetries; behavioral assessment used Griffiths Scales of Child Development (3rd edition) with factorial analysis yielding one main factor accounting for 92.4% of variance; normative modeling approach allowed control for dramatic developmental effects during pediatric age range; both age-adjusted and raw GMV analyzed to distinguish neurodevelopment from surgery-induced changes; manual masking of affected hemisphere performed on both pre- and postoperative images; symmetric T1 template constructed from normative cohort to ensure unbiased hemispheric comparisons

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This is a longitudinal study examining pre- and post-surgery GMV changes in hemispherotomy patients. The normative reference cohort (N=2115) spans ages 0.3-13.0 years from 11 multi-site datasets with varying scanner field strengths (1.5T/3T) and site numbers. For datasets with longitudinal data, only the highest quality image per subject was included, and a maximum of 100 subjects per half-year interval was used. The hemispherotomy patients had mean prescan-to-surgery intervals of 5.7±4.9 months (left) and 3.8±4.3 months (right), and surgery-to-postscan intervals of 5.0±4.1 months (left) and 4.9±4.6 months (right). Behavioral evaluations were available for only a subset of patients (19 left, 19 right). The study found that the spatial patterns of GMV changes largely mirrored each other between groups (correlation after flipping r=0.86), but brain-behavior relationships and predictive feature maps differed substantially. Etiology classifications: developmental (D), acquired (A), progressive (P). Overall GM shrinkage (negative age-adjusted GMV) was observed in majority of patients both pre- and post-surgery: 79% and 59% of left hemispherotomy patients had >80% voxels negative before and after surgery; 71% and 54% of right hemispherotomy patients had >80% voxels negative before and after surgery, respectively.
